items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: Johnny and I were so close and just wonderful, what a marvelous man and player he was.

ctx.x: That’s a fascinating backstory to all that. I want to take you back to your busy studio life. I came across one of those on-line Chuck Findley discographies, you know, the never- ending scroll. And I started to count, literally, and I said this is not going to work. But what I did see is that in 1979, according to this list, you played on 26 LPs. Like that’s more than two a month and everybody from Dolly Parton to Tom Scott. So I don’t have a question, it’s simply an observation. But I wonder if you can describe,…

Well that was wonderful actually. Well it was not really nice, I mean John Audino had passed away and I was in Germany. I was doing a little tour with Peter Herbolzheimer in Germany. And I was considering actually moving there because our son was young and I wanted him to get the culture and learn other languages other than just English. I wanted him to learn German and go to schools there. They know three or four languages everybody over there. They speak and you feel like a fool when I went over there the first…
